comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Survey: the pytest-only repo-invariant gate class is ~70 modules, not three.

Method: enumerate every `scripts/*.py` invocation in the Makefile `lint` target (23 gate
scripts + ruff/zizmor/actionlint), then sweep tests/unit, tests/scripts and tests/interfaces
for modules whose assertions are about the committed tree rather than runtime behaviour,
excluding those that merely unit-test a script `make lint` already runs.

Families found beyond the three named on this ticket:
- CI-config / workflow parity: test_ci_workflow_parity, test_verify_gate_parity,
  test_ci_actionlint_scope, test_typecheck_scope, test_make_lint_hygiene_wiring,
  test_probe_wired_into_ci, test_ci_main_push_policy, test_ci_tickets_push_policy,
  test_workflow_names, test_gate_step_tree_skew, test_git_floor_gate_tree_skew,
  test_release_workflow_pins, test_worktree_python_pin, test_git_version_floor (~20).
- Ratchets/baselines: test_complexity_baseline(+_lock_47e9), test_module_size_contract,
  test_mypy_ratchet, test_ruff_ratchet, test_config_surface_golden,
  test_packaging_dependencies.
- Whole-tree AST/policy scans: test_core_optionality, test_deprecation_registry,
  test_tests_import_convention, test_scripts_import_convention,
  test_repo_root_install_agnostic, test_nested_pytest_uniqueness,
  test_collection_isolation_guard, test_error_handling_convention,
  test_alarm_actions_terraform and others.
- Generated-artifact / docs drift: the five test_gen_*.py check-mode tests,
  test_check_docs_index, test_generated_surface_markers, test_env_registry_helper_coverage,
  test_client_template_sync, test_skill_shared_sync, plus tests/interfaces/contracts/*
  (public types, schema coverage, exit-code doc conformance, tombstone registry).

Consequence for the fix: a curated node list or a hand-applied pytest marker would be a
second list to keep in sync with this population — the same drift defect one level up, and
the class this repo already builds derive-and-diff gates (check_deploy_manifest.py) to stop.
So the resolution is the complete-by-construction one: `make verify` = lint + typecheck +
`make test`, where `make test` already carries exactly CI's DEFAULT_SUITE_MARKS
(`not integration and not external`). Nothing to enumerate, nothing to drift.

Measured on this host (worktree venv, macOS): make lint 27s, make typecheck 10s, and the
three named gate tests together 67s serial / 11.6s under `-n 4 --dist worksteal` — which is
why `make test` gains `-n auto --dist worksteal` (CI already runs the suite under xdist).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
SCOPE CORRECTION FROM THE IMPLEMENTER, and it materially changes this ticket: the pytest-only repo-invariant gate class is approximately SEVENTY modules, not the three I named. The three in my description are simply the ones that bit me in one night. The wider population includes CI/workflow parity checks, ratchet baseline-vs-tree checks, public-surface censuses, generated-artifact and docs drift gates, and whole-tree AST policy scans.

CONSEQUENCE: my proposed resolution #1 -- 'a fast make check-gates that runs exactly these ratchet/parity tests and nothing else' -- WAS WRONG. A curated node list would be a second list to keep in sync with that population, i.e. the same drift defect one level up. That is the identical error pattern this repository has produced repeatedly (740d's hand-registered fixture allowlist, 2593's hard-coded builder list, the ADR .numbers markers), and I proposed it while having just documented that pattern. Worth noting against my own judgement, not just the tree's.

CHOSEN RESOLUTION: 'make verify' = lint + typecheck + test, documented in AGENTS.md as the pre-push contract. Complete BY CONSTRUCTION -- make test already carries exactly CI's DEFAULT_SUITE_MARKS ('not integration and not external'), so nothing is enumerated and nothing can drift. make lint and the pre-commit hook are untouched, so the tight loop keeps its 27s. A Makefile target is not a ci_gate under the mechanism scanner (that kind covers scripts/check_*.py files and workflow run: steps), so no ratchet trip is expected.

Measured so far on this host (18 logical / 6 performance cores): make lint 27s, make typecheck 10s, the three named gate tests 67s serial and 11.6s under -n 4 --dist worksteal. Full-suite timing still being measured.

AC3 mechanics validated in a throwaway repo: 'git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard' sees a written-but-unstaged scripts/check_*.py that the current tracked-only listing misses, while still excluding gitignored paths -- a strictly WIDENING change that can only turn a false green red, never the reverse.

OPEN CONCERN I have raised with the implementer rather than left implicit: the full default suite is ~15-20 minutes in CI. A pre-push contract that long risks being skipped under time pressure, and a contract people skip fails exactly as badly as the false-green one it replaces -- just differently. Asked for the measured wall-clock (serial and parallel) to be documented plainly where the target is named, so a contributor plans for it rather than killing it and losing trust in the target.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ROOT-CAUSE INSIGHT FROM THE IMPLEMENTER, better than my framing and worth pinning: 'make check' ALREADY IS the fast tier (lint + typecheck), and its help text -- 'Run every check-only gate (no mutation)' -- IS ITSELF HOW THE FALSE GREEN ACQUIRED ITS AUTHORITY. A contributor reads 'every check-only gate', runs it, sees green, and reasonably concludes they have verified. The defect is not only that some gates live in pytest; it is that an existing target CLAIMS completeness it does not have.

So the fix corrects that claim rather than minting a third target name. Quoting the reasoning, which I think is right: 'Adding one would build a menu, and a menu invites picking the cheap item; deleting a false claim from an existing target shrinks the surface instead of growing it.' That is a better answer than the fast-tier option I floated, and it means my suggestion would have grown the surface that produced the problem.

MEASUREMENT DISQUALIFIED THE OBVIOUS DEFAULT: '-n auto' reached 7% in ~8 minutes on this host (18 logical / 6 performance cores), extrapolating past 100 MINUTES, because a large share of this suite forks git/bash/pytest subprocesses and oversubscribes. '-n 4 --dist worksteal' tracks to ~14 minutes; the recorded serial local suite is 1726s (~29 min). Notably the repo had ALREADY decided this -- _build-and-test.yml:780 records the explicit decision against -n auto ('over-subscribes on larger local hosts') and docs/coverage.md:42-47 already tells contributors to use -n 4. The measurement confirmed existing reasoning rather than discovering something new, which is the cheapest kind of confirmation and worth doing anyway.

PLAN REVIEW CAUGHT A REAL GAP: changing make test's scheduler without enumerating the docs that describe its serial behaviour. Now enumerated -- docs/local-dev-env.md:466 and docs/coverage.md:36-47 updated, with :470-483 deliberately left alone because it contrasts coverage tracing and tier breadth rather than scheduling, and already quotes -n 4.

AND THE IMPLEMENTER CORRECTED ITS OWN COMPLETENESS ARGUMENT: DEFAULT_SUITE_MARKS is matrix-CONDITIONAL, not the flat string first claimed. Restated precisely -- make test exactly matches the gating ubuntu-latest/py3.13 cell, is a strict superset of the other two Ubuntu cells (which add 'and not repo_policy'), and a superset of macOS's platform_compat subset. The by-construction completeness claim survives and is now accurate rather than approximately right.

So parallel-at-4 is the documented default, not an optimisation the reader must discover.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
AC2 — three RED demonstrations. Each violation was injected, measured, and reverted; the
working tree is clean of all of them.

Every one reproduces the SAME signature the bug describes: the documented local pre-flight
returns 0, and the gate CI runs returns 1.

1) Stale entry in .github/mechanism-baseline.json (injected for the demo only — never a fix):
     make lint EXIT=0
     pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py EXIT=1
     FAILED test_the_committed_baseline_matches_the_live_tree
       assert set(baseline) | admitted == live
   This is the extra bite over `--check`, which make lint DOES run: --check tolerates a
   stale entry (it buckets as 'stale', which is the ratchet's allowed direction); only the
   test asserts the union equality.

2) Dropped the `[ -f ]` guard from the 'comment-hygiene gate' step of _build-and-test.yml:
     make lint EXIT=0
     pytest tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py EXIT=1
     FAILED test_completeness_every_gate_step_is_guarded_or_marked
       .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml :: [lint] 'comment-hygiene gate' runs
       scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py with no `-f` guard and no marker

3) Added a defined, exported public symbol (`demo_surface_drift`) to rebar.__all__:
     make lint EXIT=0
     make typecheck EXIT=0
     pytest tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py EXIT=1
     FAILED test_committed_baseline_matches_live_surface
       Public API surface drift detected against the committed baseline
   Note: a first attempt used an UNDEFINED name and make lint exited 2 (ruff F822), which
   would have been a fake demonstration — the point is a tree that lint calls clean. Redone
   with a real definition placed in isort order so RUF022 also passes; only then is lint 0.

AC3 — the git-add skew, closed at the source. Wrote a new unguarded gate step referencing a
NEW, untracked scripts/check_demo_skew.py, then ran the completeness check in three states:
     OLD tracked-only listing, script UNSTAGED  -> PASSED   <- the false green
     NEW listing,               script UNSTAGED -> FAILED
     NEW listing,               script STAGED   -> FAILED
So the verdict is now a property of the tree rather than of the index. The change is strictly
widening (--cached --others --exclude-standard), so it can only turn a false green red; a
.gitignore'd path is still excluded, pinned by the new regression test.

compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

Three repo gates are enforced by pytest but not by `make lint`, so the documented local
pre-flight returns green on a tree CI rejects:

| gate | how it surfaced |
|---|---|
| `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` | change 2601 pushed red; `make lint` exit 0 |
| `tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py` | change 2600 pushed red |
| `tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py` | change 2609 pushed red; `make lint` exit 0 |

All three fired on 2026-09-04 on changes whose authors had run `make lint` and
`make typecheck` and seen them pass. The defect is the CONTRACT, not the placement: a
proxy that returns green on a tree CI will reject turns "I verified locally" into a false
statement made in good faith.

A survey (recorded in a ticket comment) puts the pytest-only repo-invariant class at
roughly seventy modules -- ratchets, baselines, public-surface censuses, workflow-parity
checks, docs/registry drift gates, whole-tree AST policy scans. Any curated subset of that
is a second list to keep in sync -- the same drift defect one level up.

## Approach

Do not curate. `make test` is `pytest -m "not integration and not external"`, which is
EXACTLY the selection CI's gating cell runs: `DEFAULT_SUITE_MARKS`
(`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:811`) is matrix-conditional, and the
`ubuntu-latest, py3.13` cell -- the one that also collects coverage -- resolves to that
same string. The other two Ubuntu cells run a strict subset of it
(`... and not repo_policy`) and macOS runs the `platform_compat` subset, so `make test` is
a superset of every cell and an exact match for the gating one.

1. **New `make verify` = `lint typecheck test`** -- named in AGENTS.md as THE pre-push
   contract. Complete by construction: no curated list, no new selection mechanism,
   nothing to drift. A Makefile target is not a `ci_gate` under the mechanism scanner
   (that kind is `scripts/check_*.py` files and workflow `run:` steps), so no mechanism is
   added.
2. **`make lint`, `make typecheck` and `.pre-commit-config.yaml` are untouched.** They
   stay the fast commit gate; commit-time cost is unchanged.
3. **No new fast-tier name is minted; the existing one is corrected.** `make check` is
   ALREADY lint + typecheck, and its help text ("Run every check-only gate (no mutation)")
   is part of how the false green got its authority. It is reworded to say plainly that it
   is the tight-loop subset and that `make verify` is what must pass before pushing.
   Adding a THIRD name would build a menu, and a menu invites picking the cheap item;
   deleting a false claim from a target that already exists shrinks the surface instead.
4. **`make test` gains `-n $(PYTEST_WORKERS) --dist worksteal`, `PYTEST_WORKERS ?= 4`.**
   CI runs the suite under xdist and local runs it serially -- itself a local/CI
   divergence of the kind this bug is about, and the reason a full local suite is slow
   enough that nobody runs it. 4 is CI's own ubuntu pin AND the value
   `docs/coverage.md:42-47` already tells contributors to use locally; the repo has an
   explicit reasoned decision AGAINST `-n auto` (it "over-subscribes on larger local
   hosts", `_build-and-test.yml:780`), which a measurement on this host confirms. So this
   aligns `make test` with existing repo guidance rather than inventing a value.
5. **The cost is documented wherever the command is named** -- `make verify`'s help text,
   AGENTS.md, `docs/local-dev-env.md`. A contributor who expects `make lint`'s ~27 s and
   gets minutes will kill it and stop trusting the target, and a contract nobody runs
   fails as badly as a green that lies.

### Consumers of `make test`'s current serial behaviour

Enumerated so none is left stale by item 4:
- `docs/local-dev-env.md:466` ("Day-to-day gates" block) -- UPDATED: gains `make verify`
  and states the scheduler and the measured cost.
- `docs/local-dev-env.md:470-483` (per-test hang budget) -- reviewed, deliberately left:
  it contrasts CI's coverage tracing and tier breadth against a local run and already
  quotes `-n 4 --dist worksteal` as CI's shape, so `make test` matching that shape makes
  the passage more accurate, not less.
- `docs/coverage.md:36-47` -- UPDATED with one sentence noting `make test` now runs that
  scheduler by default, so the hand-written invocation and the target no longer differ.

## AC3 -- the `git add` skew

`test_predates_gate_guard_parity._tracked_paths()` runs `git ls-files scripts tests docs
.github`, so it cannot see a gate file written but not yet staged: the gate reports green
before `git add` and red after, on the same working tree. It becomes `git ls-files
--cached --others --exclude-standard`, i.e. the tree as CI will see it once committed.
Strictly widening -- every path it adds is one MORE step that must carry a guard -- so it
can only turn a false green red, never the reverse.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `make verify` exists and runs `lint`, `typecheck` and `test`.
- [ ] `make verify`'s help text states its measured wall-clock cost, so the cost is visible
      from `make help` without reading any document.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and `.pre-commit-config.yaml` are unchanged in scope.
- [ ] `make check`'s help text no longer claims to run every check-only gate, and points
      at `make verify`.
- [ ] `make test` runs under `-n $(PYTEST_WORKERS) --dist worksteal` with
      `PYTEST_WORKERS ?= 4`, overridable on the command line.
- [ ] Introducing a violation of each of the three named gates in turn makes `make verify`
      fail while `make lint` still exits 0; the three RED runs are quoted on the ticket.
- [ ] `_tracked_paths()` includes untracked, non-ignored paths, so the parity gate's
      verdict does not change when a new gate file is `git add`ed; a new regression test
      pins that a written-but-unstaged path is seen.
- [ ] AGENTS.md names `make verify` as the pre-push contract, `make lint` as the
      commit-time gate, says why `make lint` alone is insufficient, and states the cost.
- [ ] `docs/local-dev-env.md` and `docs/coverage.md` agree with the new `make test`
      scheduler; the "Day-to-day gates" block lists `make verify` with its cost.
- [ ] `make verify` needs no CI provider -- make + ruff + mypy + pytest over the checkout
      only (`project.portability`).

## Testing

Every command is run from this change's own worktree with its venv first on `PATH`
(`env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" <cmd>`).

- `make lint` -- the unchanged commit gate is clean, and neither the complexity nor the
  mechanism-delta ratchet fires on this change.
- `make typecheck` -- mypy over `src/rebar` and `scripts/`.
- `make verify` -- the new contract end to end on a clean tree, timed with `time`: passes;
  the measured figure is what the help text and the docs quote.
- `pytest tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py` -- the AC3 fix and its new
  regression test.
- Three RED demonstrations, each reverted immediately after, output quoted on the ticket:
  1. add a stale entry to `.github/mechanism-baseline.json` -> `make verify` fails in
     `test_mechanism_delta.py` while `make lint` still exits 0;
  2. drop one `[ -f ... ]` guard in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` ->
     `make verify` fails in `test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py`;
  3. add a symbol to `rebar.__all__` -> `make verify` fails in `test_api_surface_gate.py`
     while `make lint` still exits 0.
- The `git add` skew demonstration: write a new unguarded gate-script reference and run
  the parity test before and after `git add` -- the verdict is identical in both states
  (on `main` it differs).

## File impact

`Makefile` (`verify`, `check` help text, `test` scheduler), `AGENTS.md`,
`docs/local-dev-env.md`, `docs/coverage.md`,
`tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py`.

file_impact.reason: add a fast target (or extend lint) that runs the three pytest-only gates -- test_mechanism_delta, test_predates_gate_guard_parity, test_api_surface_gate -- so one documented command matches what CI will reject
the mechanism-delta and module-size sections point contributors at make lint as the commit gate; that guidance must name the full pre-push set, since make lint alone returns green on trees CI rejects

AC3: the gate considers only git-tracked paths, so running it before `git add` gives a green that flips red once the new file is staged -- a second way the local signal disagrees with CI on an unchanged tree

compiled_state.title: make lint is a lying proxy for CI: three ratchet/parity gates are pytest-only, so a locally-green tree fails Verified
